subject: Zone delegation vs split-horizon: DNS & TLS approach for FinPay private endpoints

Subject: DNS + TLS for private Redwood endpoints (FinPay VPC)

Hi Aditya / Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Two follow-ups from our infra/security teams:

1) DNS ownership: we need clarity on whether Redwood expects us to delegate a subdomain in our private DNS (e.g., redwood.finpay.internal) or if we should use split-horizon records that map service FQDNs to internal IPs. Which approach do you recommend for air-gapped / VPC deployments?

2) TLS termination and client trust: we require mutual TLS from our internal clients to your private endpoints. Who manages the cert lifecycle — do we provision certificates to Redwood, or will you accept customer-supplied certs and integrate with our KMS/HSM? Also need details on rotation windows and how you validate CSRs for on-prem requests.

Can we get a technical write-up and a short call this week with your infra/security folks (ideally Karthik and Neha)? We want to finalize for our pilot starting in two weeks.

Appreciate it,
Daniel

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear questions. Short answer: both approaches are viable; we typically prefer delegated subdomains for operational simplicity and clear ownership boundaries, but split-horizon is sometimes required for strict on-prem constraints.

I've looped in Karthik (infra) and Neha (security) who can propose a concrete plan covering delegation, mutual TLS, and cert rotation. Lauren will continue to coordinate the pilot timeline.

Subject: Re: DNS + TLS for private Redwood endpoints (FinPay VPC)

All — per the ask, here is a proposed technical approach and tradeoffs. I captured pragmatic defaults that have worked for similar customers, plus options you can pick from. Attaching a simple diagram and a CSR template for the on-prem flow.

Design summary (recommended default): delegated private subdomain + customer-managed resolver
- DNS: Customer delegates a private subdomain (e.g., redwood.finpay.internal) to an internal authoritative server we can query, or provides zone-transfer-read access to a dedicated Redwood resolver in the customer's VPC. This avoids split-horizon complexity and centralizes FQDN ownership for Redwood endpoints.
- Records: Redwood publishes SRV + A/CNAME records within that delegated zone pointing to private endpoints (internal ALB or static IPs). TTLs: 300s for initial pilot, increase after stabilization.
- Resolver model: prefer in-VPC resolver (Redwood runs a small resolver pair in your VPC, bound to the delegated zone) — no public exposure, responds only to VPC CIDR. Alternative: customer maintains delegation and runs their authoritative server and pushes updates to us via secure API/webhook.

TLS & cert lifecycle: mutual TLS with support for customer-managed keys
- CSR options: we can accept either (A) customer-signed certs (you supply cert + key or just cert if you keep private key in your HSM), or (B) Redwood generates CSR via an offline workflow and you sign it with your CA. The attached csr-template.txt is the minimal required SANs and OU naming.
- Rotation: recommend automated rotation every 90 days for leaf certs; customers can opt for 180 days if their CA policy requires. We support pre-rotation windows (7 days) to ensure overlap during rollover.
- Trust anchors: for mTLS, Redwood will accept client certs signed by your CA root(s). You can either configure CA roots in our private control plane (we store only the certs, not the private keys), or we can fetch them from your internal vault via a short-lived credential exchange.
- Key management: we support customer-managed keys via two patterns: (1) you retain keys in your KMS/HSM and perform signing — we never see private keys, or (2) you give Redwood a cert chain and we store it encrypted in our KMS with access controls and audit logs.

Operational details & constraints:
- No public ACME callbacks: for air-gapped environments we use either DNS-01 in your private DNS or an offline CSR flow — ACME with http-01 won't work.
- Zone transfers: if using AXFR/IXFR, restrict to Redwood resolver IPs and limit by ACL; prefer AXFR over unsecured transfers.
- Routing failover: we'll configure multi-A records with health checks inside the VPC. If you want shaded traffic (canary), we can use weighted records and internal LB rules.
- Audit & evidence: we will provide certificate rotation logs, issuance timestamps, and CSR records for SOC2 review.

Attachments: redwood-private-dns-tls-diagram.png (diagram of delegated zone + resolver placement), csr-template.txt (CSR template with required SANs).

Open questions for FinPay:
1) Are you comfortable delegating a subdomain to Redwood's resolver pair (we run in your VPC)? If not, will you host the authoritative server and provide an API for record updates?
2) Preferred key management pattern (customer KMS vs Redwood-managed)?
3) Any internal compliance window for certificate rotations shorter than 90 days?

If this matches, we can draft the pilot runbook and lock a 2-week timeline. Happy to walk through the diagram on a short call.

Daniel — quick security confirmations and next steps: 

1) Delegation vs split-horizon: from a threat model and audit perspective, delegated private subdomain is cleaner — simpler ACLs and clearer separation of responsibilities. We'll include a short attestation clause in the pilot SOW to capture who is responsible for DNS changes.
2) mTLS & trust anchors: Redwood can accept customer-supplied root certs. Please provide the PEM(s) and preferred rotation cadence. If you want Redwood to rotate certs on your behalf, we will require a signed PoA and KMS integration details.
3) Evidence for SOC2: we'll deliver rotation logs, signed CSRs, and a short runbook excerpt showing how we validate CSR ownership (CSR contains an OU that matches your issuing policy).

Next steps: Lauren will confirm the pilot SOW language and timeline. Karthik and I will run a 30-min technical call to finalize the DNS delegation steps and the CSR exchange process.

Thanks — available tomorrow 10–11am PT for the call.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Security Lead, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference
